segments.text: When a car turns a corner, its outer wheels have to travel a longer path than the inner wheels do.
So the two wheels must spin at different speeds, and the differential makes that possible.
The engine turns a ring gear and its carrier, and small planet gears inside link the two axles.
On a curve, the planet gears start to turn, so one wheel speeds up while the other slows down.
And through it all, the carrier always moves at exactly the average speed of the two wheels.
